title: Minimum Swaps to Arrange a Binary Grid
summary: For an n x n binary grid, determine the least number of adjacent row swaps required to make all cells above the main diagonal zeros.
statement: For an n x n binary grid, determine the least number of adjacent row swaps required to make all cells above the main diagonal zeros. Return -1 if it's impossible.
constraints: grid is square and only adjacent row swaps are allowed.
After rearrangement, row i needs at least n-i-1 trailing zeros so every cell above the main diagonal is zero.
reference_solution:
def minimum_binary_grid_swaps(grid):
 n=len(grid);zeros=[]
 for row in grid:
  count=0
  for value in reversed(row):
   if value:break
   count+=1
  zeros.append(count)
 answer=0
 for row in range(n):
  need=n-row-1;candidate=row
  while candidate<n and zeros[candidate]<need:candidate+=1
  if candidate==n:return -1
  answer+=candidate-row
  zeros[row:candidate+1]=[zeros[candidate]]+zeros[row:candidate]
 return answer

hints: Count trailing zeros in every row.
For each target row from top down, find the nearest later row meeting its required zero count.
Bubble that row upward and add the traveled distance.
Choosing the nearest feasible row is exchange-optimal because every farther choice costs at least as many swaps and leaves the same multiset below.

tests.explanation: Rows with one and two trailing zeros must bubble upward, requiring three adjacent swaps.
No row has the three trailing zeros required at the top, so arrangement is impossible.
